description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2022: Uncertainty Quantification for Global Geospatial Liquefaction Models is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Weiwei Zhan, University of Central Florida (ucf.edu). Geospatial natural hazard models are simple empirical models that take advantage of broadly available geospatial proxies that capture location-specific information on geologic, geomorphologic, and hydrological characteristics and have predictive power for natural hazard predictions. Such models are useful for regional hazard assessments in both post-disaster response and pre-disaster planning phases. Coverage: Washington DC. DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-a66f-t783. Keywords: Liquefaction; Geospatial Modeling; Uncertainty Quantification; Logistic Regression; Bayesian Inference. Published 2023-04-11. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
